TRICK

TRICK (Tabletop Roleplaying Interactive Card Kit) resolves uncertain moments with Tally checks. This file is the single source for the rules: the card faces print its tables, and the browser and text versions are generated from it. The two-sided rules reference card condenses it for the table, and the playtest sheet puts a check on two pages. Design notes and simulations are in TALLY.md. Setting abilities and items are optional supplements.

Decks and suits

Each player brings two standard decks, preferably with matching backs. The four jokers are Blessed cards and wait in reserve. Aces are worth 1; numbered cards keep their values. Jacks, Queens, and Kings are interchangeable zero-value statuses of their suit, giving six of each status. Keep unused cards in a personal reserve outside play; every 10 starts there and is gained or evolved into like any other card.

SuitApproachesStatus
Strength — HeartsForce, endurance, intimidationInjury
Dexterity — SpadesEvasion, deception, improvisationStumble
Intelligence — DiamondsAnalysis, persuasion, planningStress
Weird — ClubsIntuition, empathy, invocationCurse

Choose a primary suit and a different secondary suit. They set only your starting cards, never which approach you may declare. From one deck:

  1. Take 2, 4, 6, 8 of every suit.
  2. Add A, 5, 9 of your primary suit.
  3. Add 3, 7 of your secondary suit.

Shuffle these 21 cards: seven primary, six secondary, and four in each other suit, with no statuses. Keep at least 13 ordinary cards after any removal.

The GM brings one standard deck and uses its A–10 cards for the world. Shuffle it fresh for each check.

Shared rules

  • Each player has one goal, one target, and one approach per check. You score only your own tally; tallies are never pooled or transferred. Help each other through fiction and card play.
  • Finish negotiation before drawing. During play, choose independently: no tactical discussion, card advice, or signals. A card cannot be taken back once played. Narration, rules questions, and effect declarations are welcome, but cannot coordinate tactics.
  • Printed suit determines consolation. A card's value decides only whether it wins; what you score is the world card you take.
  • Gained cards come from reserve; removed cards return there. Gained statuses enter discard immediately; gain no copy if none remain in reserve. Gain Injuries only at cleanup or between checks; Injury consequences arising during play wait for cleanup.
  • Keep your played cards in a row in play order until cleanup, unless an effect removes them or returns them to hand. Keep the world cards you take face up in a separate tally pile. Never rearrange discard; its top card is the most recently discarded.

Start a check

  1. Check each player's discard for survival before drawing or reshuffling.
  2. Agree goals, targets, stakes, and any incompatible goals or stalemates. Each player declares an approach whose suit is their trump, fixed for the check. An approach must fit the fiction: being good at sneaking does not help once you have been spotted. The GM has final say on whether an approach applies and may rule out one the situation has closed off.
  3. Size the check, then deal the world one card per trick, face up in a row, from its shuffled A–10 deck. Everyone draws the same number. Resolve draw effects as cards are drawn.
CheckTricksTargetsDefault
Standard3 per player, +13–2010

The target sets the difficulty. Each player may have their own target if their tasks differ.

TargetDifficultyExact hit7 or more short

Odds are simulated for standard checks at 2–5 players; larger tables hit more often and bust less.

Forced goals. An immediate threat can require your goal: if attacked, you must get through the attack safely. The GM sets the outcome, target, and stakes; you choose the approach. Combine simultaneous threats into one goal. New threats during play resolve through agreed consequences or a forced goal in the next check.

Play the tricks

  1. The world leads the next card in its row.
  2. Everyone chooses a card face down, then all reveal together. If your hand is empty, sit out that trick.
  3. Find the single highest card on the table, counting the world card and any Brace. If it is a player's card, and in the world card's suit or its owner's trump, it wins: its owner takes the world card into their tally pile and scores its value.
  4. Otherwise the world takes the trick: the world card is highest, the highest card is off-suit, or the top cards tie. Discard that world card.
  5. Everyone who did not win takes their card's consolation, all at once, before the next trick. Then play the next trick, until the row is used up.

The winner has to beat everyone. A high off-suit card cannot win, but it blocks: nobody beats it, so the world takes the trick. Winning is not optional: if your card is highest and on-suit, you take the world card even if it busts you. To stay safe, play low, or let someone play over you.

With the whole row visible, the real decision is which world cards to go after, and which to leave for allies. Narrate progress and setbacks within your approach; other suits can represent supporting actions.

Consolations

On a trick loss, take your losing card's consolation, including when an ally won. Resolve it independently while everyone else resolves theirs; finish before the next trick. There are no consolations after the final trick.

SuitEffect
Strength — BraceYour next card counts this card's printed value higher for beating. It never changes what you score.
Dexterity — SlipReturn this card to your hand. You lost the trick, but spent nothing.
Intelligence — RecalculateDiscard one card from hand, then draw one. You need a card to discard.
Weird — MirrorIf your next card wins, the world card scores 11 minus its value.

Brace and Mirror last for your next play only: turn the losing card sideways as a reminder. Turn a Mirrored world card upside down in your tally pile so its changed score stays visible.

Statuses

Statuses are ordinary cards worth 0. They follow every playing and winning rule, and their printed suit gives its consolation as usual: Injury Braces for 0, Stumble slips back to hand, Stress recalculates, and Curse Mirrors.

StatusEffect
Injury — StrengthTwo or more Injuries in your top N discard cards make survival your forced goal. Gain Injuries only at cleanup or between checks.
Stumble — DexterityWhen you play Stumble, discard an ordinary card from your hand, your choice.
Stress — IntelligenceWhenever you draw Stress, gain one Stress into discard. This includes redraws and cards drawn during play.
Curse — WeirdYour Curses share one supernatural compulsion. Each violation gains one Stress for every Curse not in your reserve. Remove Curses through evolution, never rest.

Record the compulsion with your first Curse; further Curses share it. An effect can name a compulsion, written gain 1 Curse (compulsion: …): a first Curse records it, and a later Curse adds it as another term of the same compulsion. Count six minus the Curses still in your reserve. Removing your last Curse ends the whole compulsion.

A Braced status can win: a 0 Braced by 6 beats a world 5, and you score the 5.

Blessed

Your four jokers are Blessed cards. Blessed is not a status: rest, evolution, and the survival scan never treat it as one.

The GM grants a Blessed for play at the table rather than anything a character did — recapping the last session, sharp roleplaying, keeping the table going. A granted Blessed moves from reserve to the top of your deck, so you draw it on your next draw. Gain no copy if none remain in reserve.

  • Blessed always takes the trick it is played in and scores the world card. It has no suit.
  • If two Blessed meet in one trick, they tie, and the world takes it.
  • A played Blessed returns to reserve, never reaching discard or a survival scan.

An unplayed Blessed cleans up like an ordinary card: it goes to discard and cycles back around, so hold one by simply not playing it. A Blessed gives no consolation.

Giving. Between tricks you may give your Blessed to another player, who takes it into hand; then draw one card yourself. Handing it over is the one signal the no-coordination rule allows — no discussion, advice, or tactical talk accompanies it. The new holder plays, holds, and cleans it up exactly as if they had drawn it.

Reshuffle, evolution, and rest

When a draw is required and your deck is empty:

  1. Evolve (optional, once per shuffle): choose two statuses of the same suit in discard and return one of them to reserve; the other remains in discard. Then either draw three random ordinary cards of that suit from reserve, keep one in discard and return the rest, or return one ordinary card of that suit from discard to reserve. Draw fewer if unavailable.
  2. Shuffle the remaining discard and continue drawing.

If your deck and discard are both empty, stop drawing.

Evolution is available on any shuffle, in preparation or mid-check. A shuffle during play does not stop the trick: set the two matching statuses aside before shuffling, so they cannot return to your deck, then finish the trick. Return one to reserve, put the other on top of discard, and resolve the rest of the evolution. Only discard enters the shuffle. Evolution removes exactly one status; its extra returned card must be ordinary.

At a GM-granted rest, remove any number of non-Curse statuses from discard. How often rest is granted is the GM's main dial for lethality, since it is the only relief from accumulated Injuries.

Resolve the check

Your tally is the total of the world cards in your tally pile, with Mirrored cards counting 11 minus their value.

Final tallyResult
Exactly the targetCritical success. You get it, and more. Return one non-Curse status from your discard to reserve.
1–3 shortSuccess, with a minor complication.
4–6 shortPartial success, with a serious complication. It may be a status.
7 or more shortFailure. Each exposed participant normally gains a fitting status.
Over the targetBust: critical failure. It goes wrong, loudly. Gain your trump suit's status.

A Curse gained on a bust names its compulsion after what went wrong. Agree any different or additional consequences before dealing. Among incompatible goals, the better result wins; on the same result, the tally closer to its target wins. A tie produces the agreed stalemate.

Resolve goals and deaths, then clean up:

  1. Return world cards to the GM's deck.
  2. Shuffle unplayed cards together and discard them.
  3. Discard your played row from earliest to latest, skipping cards already removed.
  4. Add consequence statuses on top, with Injuries last.

Survival

For living characters, count M Injuries in the top N discard cards, where N is the check's number of tricks, or all cards if fewer exist. Below two, nothing happens. At two or more, survival becomes that player's forced goal, with target 2 × M. It takes priority over other goals. A bust, or landing 7 or more short, means death; any other result is survival, with that result's complications.

Scan triggerNSurvival applies
Check start, before drawingUpcoming check's tricksIn this check
Injury gained at cleanup or between checksMost recently completed check's tricksIn an immediate check

Gain-triggered checks use the scan's N, with no rest beforehand. Lock M when it triggers; later card movement cannot change it. Use an already-recorded requirement without duplicating it.

Only check starts and Injury gains trigger scans. Other discard changes, including cleanup, wait for the next start scan. Injuries outside discard do not count.

Survival leaves Injuries in place, so a later scan can require survival again. Rest may clear them before an ordinary check.
